questions.q: As Stephen was being stoned to death by his persecutors, he fell to his knees and cried out with a loud voice. What were his final words? (Acts 7:60)
options: "Father, avenge my blood on this wicked city!"
"Lord, do not hold this sin against them."
"I will return to judge you all."
questions.explain: Reflecting the very spirit of Christ on the cross, Stephen prayed for his executioners: "And falling to his knees he cried out with a loud voice, 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them.' And when he had said this, he fell asleep."

questions.q: When Peter and John were arrested at the temple (Acts 4:1-2), the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees were greatly annoyed. What specific teaching of the apostles angered the Sadducees the most?
options: They were teaching that people should not pay temple taxes.
They were proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
They were claiming to be the new high priests of Israel.
They were declaring that the Roman government should be overthrown.
questions.explain: The Sadducees (who doctrinally denied the resurrection) were "greatly annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead." (Acts 4:2)
